channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: Degrees of financial distress: How visa cuts; high tuition crush colleges
item.description: We take a look at how a range of concerns, from the cost of a college degree to visas for foreign students, affecting colleges and universities at the start of this academic year.

item.description: The unemployment rate for 22- to 27-year-olds with higher education degrees is above the national average. Is artificial intelligence to blame?

item.title: They grew up with disability rights. Now, they're fighting to keep them

item.title: 15 states have laws that allow corporal punishment in schools. Here's where, and why
item.description: There is broad consensus among psychologists that corporal punishment can be harmful to children, but the U.S. has no federal laws banning it in public schools.

item.title: Groups sue Trump administration over new foreign student visa rule
